summary:
Amazonas is a state of Brazil, and stands under Brazil's national framework: since 2019 transphobia has been criminalised nationwide as equivalent to the crime of racism, and since 2006 Amazonas state policy prohibits discrimination based on gender identity. In March 2018 the Supreme Federal Court ruled unanimously that transgender people may change legal gender at a registry post without surgery, hormonal therapy, judicial document or medical report; registry gender changes rose 59% by 2024. Amazonas has no specific law recognising non-binary gender, and in 2022 Alex Souza de Sa became the first non-binary person recognised in the state, after rectification in Rio de Janeiro and six months of intervention by the Public Defender's Office to secure recognition in Manaus when the local notary lacked a gender-neutral marker.

Facilities access is restricted locally. On 18 October 2022 the municipality of Manaus sanctioned a law prohibiting multigender or unisex bathrooms. On 10 June 2025 Governor Wilson Lima signed Law No. 7,552 banning gender-affirming care for minors under 18.

On 10 October 2023 Amazonas Law No. 6,463 prohibited the use of gender-neutral language, non-binary dialect, or any expression deviating from standard Portuguese in the curricula and teaching materials of public and private educational institutions and in official documents of educational institutions and public offices throughout the state.

Protection machinery exists at state level. In June 2021 the Amazonas Public Defender's Office (DPE-AM) created a permanent Working Group, "Diversidade Sexual, Identidade de Gênero e Cidadania", to defend LGBTQIA+ rights, identify human rights violations in public security, train public security agents, and issue recommendations; victims of LGBTphobia are served by the Specialized Human Rights Defensoria via Disk 129 in Manaus, Monday to Friday 8h-14h. In 2021 the Amazonas State Public Defender's Office also created a Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship Working Group to address human rights violations and train security agents.

Healthcare access is under documented pressure and review. In October-November 2023 the Defensoria investigated trans access to SUS for primary care, outpatient services and hormonization, and the absence of local authorisation for transexualizing surgeries including sexual reassignment; the municipal health authority committed to dispense standardized hormone medications on Ambulatório Codajás prescriptions and to designate a reference UBS in each city zone, with the state health authority required to report on equitable integral care and hormoniotherapy gaps guaranteed under CFM Resolution No. 2.265/2019. In November 2023 the Defensoria opened a process to monitor public health services for transgender and travesti people including provision of hormones and surgeries. In August 2024 the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office recommended that the state of Amazonas guarantee comprehensive health care for the LGBTQIAPN+ population, including enabling outpatient and hospital services for the transsexualization process with sexual reassignment surgeries, with deadlines for approval and presentation to the Ministry of Health.

Violence against LGBTQ people in Amazonas is underreported and rising. Research from the Brazilian Journal of Public Security states that cases of violence against LGBTQ people in Amazonas are underreported; the Brazilian Public Security Forum indicates such cases have increased, with 43 cases registered. Amazonas led North and Center-West states with an average of 4.66 LGBTQIA+ persons murdered per million inhabitants in 2018. On 5 July 2025 Fernando Vilaca de Souza was beaten and killed in Manaus after reacting to homophobic insults, with residents reporting prior bullying; the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship, the Order of Attorneys of Brazil and federal deputy Erika Hilton expressed regret. During 2021-2022 trans persons in Amazonas faced persistent diverse violence intensifying each year while only 0.36% of crimes reported in the capital and interior involved homosexual, lesbian, bisexual and transsexual victims; police occurrence reports did not identify homophobia and transfobia motives or gender, sexuality, race and intersectionality markers, victim data were few and poorly structured with victims at times inverted to accused through faulty reports, and unprepared public agents and defective registration mechanisms produced invisibilization and lack of protection for trans victims.

Child and youth protection is documented. Since August 2024 the Amazonas Court of Justice booklet "Home is a Right!" affirms LGBTQIAPN+ adolescents facing family discrimination and expulsion from home as protected by ECA Article 17, Constitutional and ECA duties of family, society and State, Law No. 14.811/2024 criminalising bullying with penalties from fine to 4 years' imprisonment, the 2019 STF recognition of homophobia as an imprescriptible and unbailable crime, and the prohibition of conversion or "cura gay" therapies as illegal and ineffective, with legal support available from the Defensoria Especializada em Direitos Humanos. The August 2024 Amazonas Court of Justice booklet also states that conversion therapies are "prohibited and ineffective."

Same-sex marriage has been legal in Brazil since 2013 via a National Council of Justice decision following the 2011 Supreme Federal Court decision, and same-sex adoption was first allowed in Amazonas in November 2012 by an Amazonas Court of Justice judge before nationwide legalization by the Supreme Federal Court in 2015. Homosexuality has been legal in Amazonas and Brazil since 1830.
tangentialFactors:
The national layer carries Peru's separate regime: Peru does not criminalise consensual same-sex activity, but Law 32331 of 13 May 2025 bars trans people from public restrooms matching their gender identity, and the April 2025 child-protection law mandates restroom entry by "biological sex". Amazonas state and Manaus municipal rules on facilities run in the opposite direction on paper (banning unisex facilities rather than mandating birth-sex assignment), but both restrict trans people's access to facilities matching their identity in practice.

Amazonas's violence figures are raw counts and per-capita averages without a national comparison denominator in these sources; the 4.66 per million figure for 2018 is a per-capita measure limited to North and Center-West states, while the 43 registered cases and 0.36% share are raw counts from separate registries. The 0.36% figure reflects registration failure as much as incidence, since police reports did not record motive or identity markers.
localsOnly:
Amazonas residents may change legal gender at a registry post without surgery, hormonal therapy, judicial document or medical report under the March 2018 Supreme Federal Court ruling, but no non-binary or gender-neutral marker is available in the state; recognition required Public Defender's Office intervention in the one documented case. Law No. 6,463 of 10 October 2023 bars gender-neutral language and non-binary expression from educational curricula, teaching materials, and official documents of educational institutions and public offices across the state.

Residents under 18 are barred from gender-affirming care under Law No. 7,552 signed by Governor Wilson Lima on 10 June 2025. Trans residents seeking hormones or surgery must rely on SUS pathways that the Defensoria found lacked local surgical authorisation in 2023, with a designated reference UBS in each city zone and Ambulatório Codajás prescriptions for standardized hormones as the municipal commitment.

LGBTphobia victims in Manaus can reach the Specialized Human Rights Defensoria via Disk 129, Monday to Friday 8h-14h, and the DPE-AM Working Group on Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship can receive reports of public-security violations and issue recommendations. LGBTQIAPN+ adolescents expelled from home are covered by ECA Article 17 protections and can access the Defensoria Especializada em Direitos Humanos; bullying is criminalised under Law No. 14.811/2024 with penalties up to 4 years' imprisonment.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Wikipedia-sourced claim that Amazonas state policies prohibit discrimination based on gender identity since 2006 and that transphobia has been criminalised nationwide as equivalent to racism since 2019 is stated without citation to the underlying state instrument or STF decision in the inventory; the specific Amazonas policy text and its scope are unresolved.

Whether Law No. 7,552 of 10 June 2025 has been challenged in court, and whether the August 2024 Federal Public Prosecutor's Office recommendations on trans surgery services have been implemented, are not sourced here. The inventory does not document enforcement of the Manaus unisex-bathroom ban or of Law No. 6,463's language prohibition against individuals.

The 43 registered cases of violence against LGBTQ people in Amazonas are attributed to the Brazilian Public Security Forum without a year, and the relationship between that figure and the 0.36% share of reported crimes is unresolved. Amazonas-specific data on trans people murdered, as distinct from LGBTQ people generally, is not available in these sources.
